content_of_post_to_comment:
I’ve been a night owl my entire life and until you’re done with school this type of schedule is extremely rewarding. You come home after school and activities, grind your work until it’s very late, repeat. I believe it’s what has made me successful up until now (and I did grad school so I also worked that way until I no longer had classes).
Now I am 27 and I’m like wtf???? Each day I have some meetings or appointments and it’s not too much technically, but they can fall anywhere between 9:30am to 5:30pm. Then, sometimes my friends make plans after work and I can’t say no to all of them or I’ll be a hermit.
But the thing is I actually do have flexibility to work anytime I want to between those timeframes but I’m not sure how to build my day when the interruptions from work can be 9-5 and from external to work obligations from 5 onwards. I’m honestly not sure how people typically weave in and out of work with constant interruptions.

The key for me is that I don’t \*have\* to stop working at 5. Nobody said stop working at 5, and nobody is watching me and making sure I’m working at 9 either, so I’m not tied down in the same way corporate work is. But I’m still extremely frustrated.

My dream schedule would be:
\- wake up sometime between 9-11
\- light work for a few hours
\- in the afternoon, take a few hours break to work out, meditate, shower, eat lunch, take a nap
\- leave around 3pm, bringing dinner with me, and go somewhere I can actually hole myself up and grind until around midnight
\- then come home and watch a show, get ready for bed, repeat.

It’s actually a lot of work hours when you think about it. I just really miss having the luxury to get lost in my work.

But the obligation to show up and be at meetings, and cut in and out of work constantly while also maintaining life is just confusing me to hell and I don’t like it. I also have ADHD and have thrived thus far due to hyper focus.

So what do I even do at this point???

I had tried to compromise by having an 8pm cutoff to my work and saying I have to fit in my morning routine, getting to work, one workout, lunch, any meetings, appointments, or social plans, and to work any time those things aren’t happening. If any of the plans or meetings end before 8pm I have to get back to work and after 8pm I cannot work anymore, full stop. But idk how I feel about this. It’s still such a repeated start and stop to my work. It still doesn’t allow me to tap into my natural grind.

Does anyone have suggestions when they are a night owl, have freedom and flexibility to work but also have obligations that fit the common 9-5?
comment: I relate to the struggle of losing those long uninterrupted stretches. One thing that helped me was realizing hyperfocus is a great tool, but it makes a terrible default schedule when adult life adds friction. I started treating deep work blocks like appointments instead of waiting for the perfect flow state. Have you tried protecting just one or two no-interruption windows each week?
